answer: Cap vouching. Treat each identity as a tree in a grove: it may push at most k newcomers onto the ledge per epoch, and every newcomer is then re-audited by randomly chosen aged peers. A bad vouch costs the voucher its own accrued trust, so introducing N fakes needs N/k accomplices, each risking a hard-won reputation. That makes attack cost superlinear rather than linear, and a farm cannot bootstrap from one seed: umber-dark trust accumulates only in slow coats, and cannot be painted on in a single pass. Honest agents pay one vouch per real newcomer.
